parole.significato: A type of old snow which has gone through multiple thaw and refreeze cycles and thus is made of numerous small icy grai…
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Firn, from Alemannic German firn (“last year's”), from Old High German firni (“old”), from Proto-West Germanic [Term?], from Proto-Germanic *firnijaz, *fernaz (“foregoing, previous”), from Proto-Indo-European *per- (“forth, forward, across, through”); cognate with Old English fy

parole.significato: Any sediment, dominated by silt, of eolian (wind-blown) origin.
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Löss (“yellowish-gray soil”), from Alemannic German lösch (“loose”). Cognate with German los and English lease.

parole.significato: A coup d'état; an illegal effort to forcibly overthrow the current government.
parole.testo: Borrowed from German Putsch, from Alemannic German Putsch (“knock, thrust, blow”), of imitative origin.

parole.significato: A wandering on foot; an idle and leisurely walk; a ramble; a saunter.
parole.testo: Borrowed from German strollen, seemingly from Alemannic German strollen; related to Strolch (“vagabond; rascal”) and strolchen.

parole.significato: An endangered species of ibis, the northern bald ibis, Geronticus eremita.
parole.testo: From German Waldrapp, from German Wald (“forest”) + Alemannic German Rapp (“raven”), the latter cognate with German Rabe, English raven.
